purpose: Test-retest fixture for the v15.6 casesAudit pass. Ten fixed MCQ items with reference classifications, run repeatedly under identical settings to measure whether one configuration scores an item the same way twice.
why: No published figure establishes audit reliability for this build. The June 2026 reliability study (Simms, Hensel, Cavanaugh, Fox & Kumar, Nurse Educ Pract 94:104897) tested five OpenAI and two Anthropic configurations and zero Gemini, and lists intra-rater reliability as unmeasured while calling it a foundational property for operational use. Nothing here may be compared to any published ICC or accuracy figure.
referenceStandardCaveat: The reference classifications below were authored in-house, the same limitation the source papers acknowledge of themselves: the authors wrote the rubric, the items, and the reference classifications, so agreement measures alignment with one interpretive framework rather than an external standard. The 'sound' and 'borderline' labels are judgment calls. Only the two seeded items carry a defect that is mechanically unambiguous, which is why missed-defect rate is the metric to trust most and 'false fatal on a sound item' the one to trust second.

bands.sound: Expected to PASS. A FAIL here is a false fatal failure.
bands.seeded: Contains exactly one deliberately injected defect on the named criterion. Expected to FAIL on that criterion. A PASS here is a missed defect.
bands.borderline: Genuinely improvable but not disqualifying. NO expected verdict. These exist to confirm the gate does not discriminate at the moderate/high boundary — inconsistent results here are expected behaviour, not a regression. Do not tune toward them.

items.note: Clean stem, four parallel options of similar length, one defensible key, no stem/key vocabulary repetition.

items.note: DEFECT: negatively constructed stem ('all of the following EXCEPT'), which criterion 1 names explicitly. Options are otherwise clean and of even length, so this item should fail on criterion 1 and nothing else.
